title: Customer Alpha — integration call notes and next steps
content:
Call: Customer Alpha integration scoping (2026-03-29)
Attendees: Samir Desai (Redwood CS), Leah Gomez (Redwood Solutions), Rory Chen (Redwood SRE), Julia Fernandez (Customer Alpha CTO), Marcus Bell (Customer Alpha infra)

Summary:
- Customer Alpha is evaluating Redwood Dedicated or Private for a regulated payments flow. Primary drivers: data isolation (must not leave their VPC), predictable latency for 2k TPS inference bursts, and compliance with their internal audit (KMS/HSM).
- They currently run a mix of synchronous user-facing prompts and async batch scoring for risk models. Peak token rate estimate: ~1.5M tokens/min during campaign windows. Typical latencies required: 95th <= 120ms for single-turn gen on short prompts (<=128 tokens).
- Risk appetite: prefer a Dedicated reservation with private peering; Private (on-prem) considered for Q4 if audit requires it.

Key requirements (from Julia/Marcus):
- VPC peering + private control plane (no public internet access)
- Support for customer-managed KMS; HSM integration is a hard requirement for keys to sign logs
- RBAC + SSO (SAML 2.0) with SCIM provisioning from Okta
- Throughput: baseline reserved capacity to handle 500 TPS with burst to 2k TPS for 10-30 minutes. Autoscaling policy must be predictable and deterministically bounded for cost forecasting.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 120ms for short prompts; fallbacks to cheaper model allowed but must maintain semantic equivalence tests in rollout.
- Audit/logging: token-level cost and latency traces retained for 90 days; exportable to their Splunk instance.

Technical notes / gotchas raised on call:
- Marcus: network egress rules are strict. We'll need to validate if Dedicated with private peering meets their no-internet policy or we need Private deployment (control plane in their VPC). Follow-up: confirm whether Managed NAT is allowed for control plane metadata calls.
- Leah: model size and quantization tradeoffs. For their latency target we may need 4-bit quant or tensor-parallel placements on A100s. Confirm model family (they plan to use an open LLM v2 variant) and provide benchmark numbers for our runtime.
- Rory: caching strategy — many requests are prefix-similar (customer metadata + templated prompts). Suggest prefix KV caching and a warm-up plan before campaign windows. Need to quantify cache hit ratio expectation.
- Security: HSM integration timeline unknown; coordinate with our Security team and their KMS vendor. This is gating for production.

Open questions (to resolve in next week):
1) Which exact model checkpoint do they want to serve? (Customer to confirm model name/version)
2) Can their infra team accept Redwood-managed control plane but with private peering, or do they require fully private control plane? (Marcus to confirm by 2026-04-02)
3) HSM vendor details and certs — list of supported HSMs from Redwood security (action: Samir to pull existing HSM integration doc)
4) Expected token length distribution during peak campaigns (Customer to provide sample logs)
5) SSO connector details (Okta org URL, SCIM attributes)

Immediate next steps / action items:
- Samir: send integration checklist + initial Dedicated sizing worksheet (baseline 500 TPS / burst 2k) by 2026-03-31. (ACTION)
- Leah: run quick perf benchmarks (internal) for the candidate open-LM family on our 4-bit quant path and provide 95p latency numbers for 128-token prompts by 2026-04-02. (ACTION)
- Rory: draft recommended caching + warm-start policy for campaign windows; include estimated hit rates and cost impact by 2026-04-03.
- Marcus/Julia (Customer): provide model checkpoint name and example prompt distribution + Okta SAML metadata by 2026-04-02.
- Security (cc: Leah): Samir to intro Customer security contact to Redwood security to discuss HSM/KMS scope; schedule technical deep-dive.

Risks and mitigation:
- HSM gating: if HSM/procurement timeline slips, propose temporary compromise: use customer-managed KMS without HSM for initial pilot with strict audit; require sign-off from their audit team.
- Latency miss on peak: propose traffic shaping and a two-tier rollout (canary -> gradual ramp) with automatic fallback to a slightly smaller model to preserve latency. Need to surface quality regression monitoring.

Notes to self:
- Use the Dedicated sizing template (internal) but flag as optimistic until we get token distribution.
- Link to similar Customer X engagement where Private control plane was required — helpful for procurement questions.
- Remember to capture Splunk ingestion format for logs (they want CSV + JSON events).

Follow-up meeting: Proposed 30-45m technical deep dive week of 2026-04-06 to cover peering, HSM, and perf benchmarks. I proposed Leah + Rory + Samir + their infra/security technical leads.

File attachments to add to Drive (post-call):
- dedicated-sizing-worksheet.xlsx (draft)
- perf-benchmarks-openlm-v2.md (internal)
- hsm-integration-checklist.pdf
